date: DRAFT, set to the day of the founder ruling
title: The PRD workspace keeps OpenRouter with our own tool loop; Managed Agents is not adopted; the reservation covers the whole request
decision: Every PRD model call (main, section and NGO side chats, the completion check, and the planning package's generations) stays on OpenRouter from edge functions, with our own tool loop. The reservation covers the whole request, including every tool step; each generation settles once by its identifier; the unspent remainder is released when the request ends unless a cost is pending; a request the provider rejects before any generation releases its whole reservation; a pending cost is reconciled through the generation lookup. The model's tools run in the edge function: chat tools write PRD state through the backend's role checks, and only the planning package writes the repository and Linear, through the task-management writer (REQ-026). Claude Managed Agents is not adopted for the PRD workspace; revisit it for the planning package only if a package step cannot finish inside one edge function call or the package must run code against the repository. The direct Claude API path is the fallback if OpenRouter's reported cost does not match its generation lookup in a live run, or if Anthropic models through OpenRouter lose prompt caching.
evidence: loop/items/ai-path/memo.md and loop/items/ai-path/spike/. Measured on the local stack and the Supabase edge runtime: the path-neutral ledger (hold across a tool loop, settle once per receipt, pending remainder, release on rejection, empty id refused, overrun shown, short funds refused, exactly three of five concurrent holds won in 20 of 20 rounds) and no model key in the browser stream on all three paths. Read: OpenRouter usage accounting (usage.cost per generation, /generation lookup, no markup on inference), Managed Agents usage and credential handling, the Anthropic cost report (daily, by workspace, no per-message lookup), the stub paid-Discovery fuel functions, the Discovery port's limits, the founder-approved wiring plan of 2026-10-14, and the Supabase 400-second limit. Not measured: live streaming, tool calls, cost and latency. Adversarial review ran with one model; the Codex and Grok lanes dropped out unauthenticated.
supersedes: Nothing. It refines d93's OpenRouter settlement with the whole-request reservation and the release rule.
